fig1_central_limit.svg: Central Limit Theorem via sample_uniform_sum: the sum of $m$ independent $U(0,1)$ variables, standardized to zero mean and unit variance, against the $N(0,1)$ density (normal_pdf, dashed). One uniform is flat, two make a triangle, and by $m=12$ the histogram is already an excellent Gaussian — why errors built from many small independent effects come out normally distributed.
fig2_least_squares.svg: Ordinary least-squares fit from least_squares_line to noisy data $y=2+3x$ (Gaussian noise $\sigma=0.7$). The routine returns the slope and intercept with $1\sigma$ uncertainties; the shaded region is the $\pm1\sigma$ confidence band $s\sqrt{1/n+(x-\bar x)^2/S_{xx}}$ for the fitted line, tightest at the data's centroid. Recovered slope and intercept match the truth within error.
